evidence: Cic. Fam. 9.26.3: nōn multī cibī hospitem accipiēs, multī jocī
Hor. S. 2.6.80–81: rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō
terms.comment: Of a host and his guests: to receive and treat them.

evidence: Liv. 3.26.11: trēs obviam ēgressī fīliī excipiunt
terms.comment: Of coming out to meet someone and taking them in.
Of taking someone in under one’s roof.

phrases.latin: quā rē nihil est quod adventum nostrum extimēscās; nōn multī cibī hospitem accipiēs, multī jocī.
phrases.english: so there is no reason to dread my coming: you will be receiving a guest of little food and many jokes.

phrases.latin: ōlim rūsticus urbānum mūrem mūs paupere fertur accēpisse cavō, veterem vetus hospes amīcum
phrases.english: once upon a time, they say, a country mouse welcomed a town mouse to his poor hole, an old host his old friend

phrases.latin: trānsvectumque trēs obviam ēgressī fīliī excipiunt
phrases.english: when he had crossed, his three sons came out to meet him and took him in
